Phased developments shall not relieve a developer of such responsibility. Subsequent phases of development which could be constructed to be one project shall cause retroactive institution of this requirement for the total of all lots or sites in all phases even if, individually, each phase of development is less than the 50 site or lot threshold. Location of the required recreation area shall be centrally located and convenient to the development if less than the 50 site or lot threshold. Such required recreation area shall be centrally located and convenient to the development, and shall be subject to approval of the location and suitability by the planning commission and board of commissioners.
(6) A mobile home development, including a mobile home park or subdivision, shall be located only on property located in districts zoned as R-4 residential districts under the zoning ordinance (appendix A to this Code), except where a mobile home subdivision is part of a planned unit development district (PUDD) under the zoning ordinance (appendix A to this Code).

840:
(a) Mobile home parks.
(1) The minimum size lot, tract or parcel of land to be used for a mobile home park shall not be less than five acres in size, and shall contain at least eight mobile home spaces or stands, as defined in subsection (a)(2) of this section.
(2) The minimum size mobile home site, space or stand (the lot or area to be occupied by each mobile home with required electrical and other utility hookups) within a mobile home park shall contain not less than 6,500 square feet of area. Only one mobile home shall be placed on each lot.
(3) The minimum lot width for each mobile home site, space or stand shall be 100 feet.
(4) A mobile home shall not occupy in excess of one-third of its respective lot or site area. The accumulated occupied area of the mobile home and any accessory structures on a mobile home lot shall not exceed two-thirds of the respective lot or site area.
(5) Mobile homes are encouraged to be placed parallel or angled to the street.
(6) No mobile home shall be located within 25 feet of any exterior boundary of the mobile home park or within 25 feet of any street or accessway boundary or right-of-way line.
(7) Each mobile home stand, site or lot shall have a concrete patio at least four inches thick, with minimum dimensions of ten feet by ten feet.
(8) Accessory structures customarily incidental to residential uses are allowed on each mobile home site or lot, but shall not be located closer than ten feet to any lot or site boundary line or within 25 feet of any street or accessway boundary or right-of-way line. Such structures shall be screened from the view of any street or accessway, whether by the mobile home itself, if appropriate, or by appropriate plantings.
(9) Each mobile home park shall have approved internal water, sewer and underground electrical systems. Approval of internal water, sewer and electrical systems shall require submission and approval of plans and specifications and acceptance of facility construction by the city, the county health department, the state department of natural resources and any other agencies necessary to comply with all applicable state and local laws and regulations. Whenever a municipal water system shall be located within 1,000 feet of any portion of the mobile home park boundary, the owner shall be required to connect such internal water system to the appropriate municipal system at the owner's expense. Whenever a municipal sewer system shall be located within 500 feet of any portion of the mobile home park boundary, the owner shall be required to connect such sewer system to the appropriate municipal system at the owner's expense. In order to be considered as a part and extension of the city's municipal water system, upon the request of the city, the owner of such mobile home park shall convey by deed, easement or other instrument acceptable to the city such internal water system that is connected to the city's municipal water system. Similarly, in order to be considered as a part and extension of the city's municipal sewer system, upon the request of the city, the owner of such mobile home park shall convey by deed, easement or other instrument acceptable to the city such internal sewer system that is connected to the city's municipal sewer system. The city may require such conveyance of any such internal water system or internal sewer system prior to acceptance of such systems as a part and extension of the city's municipal systems and prior to the connection of any such internal water system or internal sewer system to the city's municipal systems.
(10) Garbage and trash disposal shall be by approved public means, if reasonable, and in any instance, shall be acceptable to the city and shall comply with any applicable state and local laws and regulations. Any solid waste collection stands utilized shall be screened from conspicuous view.
(11) Off-street parking spaces meeting accepted engineering standards shall be provided at the rate of at least two car spaces for each mobile home site or lot within the mobile home park. To meet such requirement, common parking areas may be designed, but must be generally accessible and convenient. In every instance, at least one off-street parking space shall be provided on each mobile home site or lot.
(12) Each mobile home park shall have abutting frontage on a public street, at its entrance, of not less than 75 feet. Entrances shall be landscaped and shall provide safe and convenient all-weather vehicular access with direct connections to a public street with a permanent easement or right-of-way of not less than 50 feet, including a graded width of at least 40 feet or a paved width of at least 22 feet. Design standards of such requirement shall meet the standards established by the city for similar developments and city streets. Signs, landscaping and lighting should be integrated in a coordinating manner and be harmonious to the entrance.
(13) Safe and convenient vehicular access to each mobile home site or lot shall be streets, driveways or other accessways, which shall be kept open and shall be constructed and maintained in such a manner as to be passable to vehicular traffic under all weather conditions. Any streets, driveways or other accessways shall have easements or rights-of-way of at least 30 feet if designed for one-way traffic, and at least 40 feet otherwise. Streets, driveways or other accessways shall have at a minimum graded width of 30 feet or pavement widths of 20 feet, unless a street serves 15 mobile homes or less, in which case it may have a graded width of 18 feet. No part of any street, accessway or driveway easement or right-of-way shall be included in the required individual mobile home site or lot area. Design standards of such requirement shall meet the standards established by the city for similar developments and city streets.
(14) A buffer strip shall be located adjacent to each exterior property line of the mobile home park, and shall not be included within any individual mobile home lot. The required width of the buffer strip shall vary according to the screening contained within the buffer strip. If plantings are used as screening, such buffer strip shall be at least 50 feet wide, with approved visually solid year-round plantings which will grow to at least six feet in height within two years. If visually solid earth mounds or berms are used, then the screenings shall be at least six feet in height and landscaped, and the required width of the buffer strip shall be reduced to a minimum of 25 feet.
(15) Such storm drainage improvements and facilities as are necessary, safe and adequate for the mobile home park, as determined by the city, shall be provided. Where a mobile home park is traversed by any existing or proposed public watercourse, drainageway, channel or stream there shall be provided a stormwater easement or drainage right-of-way of at least ten feet along each side of the channel or watercourse for the purpose of widening, deepening, relocating, improving, maintaining or protecting such drainage easement.
(16) It shall be the duty and responsibility of the owner or his authorized agent to keep the mobile home park in a reasonably clean and sanitary condition, at all times, subject to approval of the city, and to maintain and keep in good repair all required facilities and accessways. All wastewater from washing machines and other sources shall be discharged into the sanitary sewer system, and under no circumstances shall such wastes be discharged onto the ground, into drainageways or streams.
(17) Internal water, sewer, street and private drainage systems shall be property of the owner and shall not be dedicated to the city.
(18) No part of any mobile home park shall be used for nonresidential purposes, except such uses that are approved by the planning commission and board of commissioners, as necessary, for the management and maintenance of the park or the wellbeing of the park residents.
(19) No mobile home park shall be converted into a mobile home subdivision without a new permit and until all additional requirements for a mobile home subdivision are compiled with.
(b) Mobile home subdivisions.
(1) The minimum lot size, excluding rights-of-way, shall contain not less than 7,500 square feet, and only one mobile home may be placed on each lot where no other dwelling exists.
(2) The minimum lot width shall be 100 feet.
(3) A mobile home shall not occupy in excess of one-third of its respective lot area. The accumulated occupied area of the mobile home and any accessory structures on the lot shall not exceed 50 percent of the respective lot area.
(4) Mobile homes are encouraged to be placed parallel or angled to the street. No mobile home is to be placed within five feet of a property boundary line, unless the length of the mobile home and the lot width is such that this requirement must be waived in order to achieve parallel placement. However, no mobile home shall be placed within 30 feet of any permanent type of building on adjacent lots, as measured to the closest point.
(5) Mobile homes shall be set back at least 25 feet from any street right-of-way boundary line.
(6) Accessory structures customarily incidental to residential use are allowed on a mobile home subdivision lot, but shall not be located closer than ten feet to any property line or within 25 feet of any street right-of-way boundary line. Such structures shall be screened from conspicuous view of any street by either the mobile home itself, if appropriate, or by appropriate plantings.
(7) The frame, axles, wheels, crawl space storage area and utility connections of all mobile homes in mobile home subdivisions shall be concealed from view by either low profiling (the lowering of the mobile home to the ground by depressing the supporting foundation below grade), earth berming, skirting or a permanent foundation. Skirting shall be of durable all-weather construction as manufactured especially for the purpose of covering the undercarriage area, and shall be installed and fastened in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions.
(8) Each mobile home in the mobile home subdivision shall have approved public water, public sewer, and underground electrical connections if such public service is available at any exterior boundary of the mobile home subdivision.
a. Water connection is required if such public service is located within 1,000 feet of the mobile home subdivision.
b. Sewer connection is required if such public service is located within 500 feet of the mobile home subdivision.
c. Electric connection is required if such public service is located within 100 feet of the mobile home subdivision.
The mobile home subdivision developer shall have required public water and sewer systems installed at the developer's expense, subject to approval of plans and specifications and acceptance of facility construction by the city. Whenever public systems services are not reasonably available (more than the prescribed distance listed in 62-38(b)(8)), then each lot shall have a water source and sewage disposal means approved and accepted by the city, the county health department, the state department of natural resources and any other agencies necessary to comply with all applicable state and local laws and regulations.
(9) Two off-street parking spaces, meeting accepted engineering standards, shall be provided on each mobile home lot and shall be connected to the abutting public street with a driveway at least ten feet wide.
(10) Each lot in a mobile home subdivision must front a public street dedicated to and accepted by the city. Each such street shall have a right-of-way of not less than 50 feet, and shall be developed in accordance with the subdivision ordinance (appendix B to this Code). The design standards of such street shall meet the standards established by the city for city streets.
(11) The boundary corners of each mobile home lot shall be clearly marked on the ground by permanent, flush, one-half-inch diameter by 18-inch-long steel pins or similar markings. The location of lot corners on the ground shall be precisely the same as shown on accepted plans. Precise engineering by a state registered surveyor of lot lines and corners is required for plan, lot location and recording of deeds.
(12) Such street lighting systems, storm drainage improvements and facilities as are necessary, safe and adequate for the mobile home subdivision, as determined by the city, shall be installed by the developer. Where a mobile home subdivision is traversed by any existing or proposed watercourse, drainageway, channel or stream there shall be provided a stormwater easement or drainage right-of-way of at least ten feet along each side of the channel or watercourse for the purpose of widening, deepening, relocating, improving, maintaining or protecting such drainage easement.
(13) A landscaped buffer strip shall be located adjacent to each exterior property line of the mobile home subdivision. The width of such required buffer strip shall vary according to the screening contained within the buffer strip. If landscaped plantings only are used, the buffer strip shall be at least 50 feet wide and contain visually solid landscaped screening at least six feet high, approved by the city. If visually solid earth mounds or berms are used, then they shall be at least six feet in height and landscaped, and the required width of the buffer strip shall be reduced to a minimum of 25 feet. Such buffer strip shall be dedicated as a permanent easement and deed restriction, but shall remain in the ownership of the adjacent property owners for their limited use, enjoyment and maintenance, with further provision that no permanent structures of any type may ever be erected within the buffer strip. The portions of a lot within a buffer strip shall not be utilized when determining whether total lot size meets minimum requirements of this article. The remainder of a lot, excluding the buffer strip, shall at least meet the minimum lot size requirements under this article, but in no instance shall it be less than the equivalent square footage of the average of adjacent subdivision lots without the buffer strip.
(14) Entrances to mobile home subdivisions shall be landscaped and signed in a harmonious and visually attractive manner.
(15) No provisions of this article shall be construed to relieve the developer of meeting additional provisions or requirements required of all subdivisions under the subdivision regulations (appendix B to this Code) of the city.
(16) No part of any mobile home subdivision shall be used for nonresidential purposes, except such uses that are approved by the planning commission and board of commissioners, as necessary, for the management and maintenance of the subdivision or the wellbeing of the mobile home park residents.
(c) Individual lots.
(1) Mobile homes may not be used on individually owned lots for residential purposes, other than on lots within an approved mobile home subdivision.
(2) No temporary permits for mobile homes in residential zones shall be allowed, except in the case of a natural disaster or other act of God where a single-family residence was destroyed for a period not to exceed 90 days. Such temporary permit shall expire and may not be renewed unless a building permit for reconstruction of the single-family residence is issued within the 90-day period. Upon issuance of a building permit, the temporary permit may be extended for the length of construction or a period not to exceed six months, whichever is less.
(3) A mobile home may be used for office or security space, on a temporary basis, for the length of construction only, upon city permit, in nonresidential zones, upon a lot for which a building permit for permanent construction has been issued.
